title: How to Lower Your Startup Recruiting Budget (October 2026)
summary: Slash startup recruiting costs in October 2026 by switching to a free ATS, fractional recruiters, and employee referral programs.
body_markdown:
[Recruiting spend](https://www.dover.com/) tends to climb fastest when a startup can least afford it: agency fees tied to a percentage of salary, paid software subscriptions, and job board postings all arrive before a single hire starts. Lowering that spend without slowing hiring comes down to a handful of changes in tooling, sourcing, and how roles get staffed, each covered below.


**TLDR:**


-


Agency recruiters typically charge 15-30% per hire, so three hires can cost $45-90k in fees alone.


-


A free ATS can replace paid platforms costing thousands, with no drop in candidate tracking quality.


-


Employee referrals tend to produce the shortest time to hire and highest quality applicants.


-


Remote work cuts office costs and widens your candidate pool without added recruiting spend.


-


Some tools combine a free ATS with on-demand recruiting support, keeping hiring costs predictable.


## What Does a Recruiting Budget Typically Look Like?


The “typical” recruiting budget can vary from company to company, but many startups have to funnel money into the same places. The typical recruiting budget likely includes:


-


**Internal costs** - These costs might be internal recruiters you have on staff, your applicant tracking system, sourcing tools, and other software your team might need.


-


**External costs** - These could include job board postings, ads, background checks, relocations for new hires, and recruiting agencies who usually charge a 15-30% fee.


Let’s put it this way: You need to hire 3 mid-level employees with a budget of $100k for each of them. If you have a recruiting agency handle them, you’re looking at $45-90k just for your[recruiting agency fees](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-hourly-rate-vs-agency-fees) . And many startups are spending more.


There’s a better way.


## Ways to Cut Back on Hiring Spend as a Startup Founder


When you start researching ways to cut costs on recruiting, you’ll likely run into a lot of advice to invest in software and tools to help you save time and (eventually money) on your recruiting processes. This can work, but you’re looking at spending more to save more, which can be hard on a company that’s already looking to minimize hiring spend.


Instead, you can cut back on recruitment costs by shifting strategies and using free tools. Let’s take a look at some of the best ways to cut costs:


### 1. Use a Free Applicant Tracking System (ATS)


According to a[survey by GetApp](https://www.getapp.com/resources/recruitment-strategies-report-2017/) , a whopping 86% of recruiters said an ATS has increased the speed at which they hire candidates and 78% say it improved the quality of candidates they hire. So it shouldn’t be a question of “if” you need an applicant tracking system. The question is, which one do you use?


Applicant tracking systems can vary widely in price, with many companies spending thousands if not tens of thousands, on these platforms. The truth is, that most of these companies could be spending $0 on their ATS and still get world-class features.


That’s where[Dover](https://www.dover.com/ats) comes in. Dover is a free ATS that helps hiring teams stay organized, post jobs to 50+ job boards, source candidates from LinkedIn with a free Chrome extension and get a bird’s-eye view into your entire hiring pipeline. On the Premium plan, AI applicant scoring helps you review applicants 10x faster and make sure you never ghost a top candidate again. The free plan doesn’t cost a dime.


### 2. Hire Freelancers and Contractors


Outsourcing your recruiting can be a huge cost saver for startups. With freelancers and contractors, you can access high-level expertise and take the pains of the recruiting process off your plate.


Usually, the problem with hiring freelance recruiters is how cost-prohibitive it can be for startups, with agency recruiters and other contractors often taking a considerable amount of money for each hire. That’s where more flexible and affordable solutions like Dover’s Recruiting Partners can help.


Dover’s Recruiting Partners are priced for startups, with no minimum commitment and the ability to pause at any time. An ATS handles tracking, scheduling, and candidate communication, but sourcing capacity or a specialized role is often where software alone stops being enough. At that point, a full-cycle[fractional recruiter](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiting-guide) can work inside the same pipeline, so the hiring team and the recruiter see the same candidates and avoid duplicate outreach. Verified founder reviews of each recruiter in the marketplace make it possible to check their record on startup roles before you engage.


### 3. Use Sourcing Software


The right[sourcing software](https://www.dover.com/sourcing) allows you to find qualified candidates in your sleep. And like applicant tracking systems, you can start with free tools: Dover’s free Chrome extension sends personalized email outreach straight from LinkedIn profiles, and Dover’s Sourcing Autopilot helps you find great candidates and use AI to generate a highly personalized email based on their profile.


The first touch matters most when contacting top candidates, and Dover’s Sourcing Autopilot takes all the guesswork out of the process. This way, you can reach out to the most qualified candidates in seconds.


### 4. Offer Internships and Part-Time Positions


SHRM’s[2025 Talent Trends research](https://www.shrm.org/topics-tools/research/2025-talent-trends) found that 69% of organizations offer internship programs, and 78% of HR professionals rate them as somewhat or very effective at addressing talent shortages. These positions are cost-effective compared to full-time hires. They also give you a chance to bring on future top talent early and grow them within the company.


Internships and part-time positions allow both the company and the hire to decide if the arrangement is a good fit. And if things don’t work out in either direction, the cost is far less than onboarding and offboarding full-time positions. It’s a win-win for everyone.


### 5. Transition to Remote Work


[Buffer’s 2023 State of Remote Work report](https://buffer.com/state-of-remote-work/2023) found that 98% of respondents would like to work remotely, at least some of the time. Chances are, your employees want to work remotely, and startup founders should want the same thing. For one, offering remote work or hybrid work is clearly a priority for a huge portion of the workforce. Remote work also gives you a much wider talent pool, letting you find top candidates all over the world.


Remote work can lead to considerable cost savings too. Startups often feel pressured to offer cool or trendy office spaces in expensive areas. But why spend the money when your employees would prefer to stay home anyway? The continued industry-wide transition to remote work isn’t slowing down anytime soon, and it’s not hard to see why.


### 6. Encourage Employee Referrals


If you value the people you have, you probably value their opinions too. There’s a good chance that your employees know someone who could be an asset to the company, so encouraging employee referrals is an easy and cost-effective way to increase your candidate pool.


Of course, this means you should offer incentives like a bonus if a referral makes it through the hiring process. But that bonus is far less than you would have to pay a recruiter, and the quality of the candidate is probably higher. Plus, you increase morale because you give an employee a bonus and they have someone they like on the team.


There’s also the fact that GetApp’s recruiter survey on referrals also said that many recruiters found referrals led to the shortest time to hire and the best quality applicants compared to other methods like job boards, recruitment agencies and social media. A 2020[Clutch survey on referral programs](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/55-of-companies-say-employee-referrals-reduce-hiring-cost-strategy-could-decrease-hr-costs-when-economy-reopens-301044969.html) also found that 55% of companies with a referral program say it reduced their hiring costs.

## How Dover Fits Into a Lower Recruiting Budget


Built for startups that need to hire without dedicated recruiting headcount, Dover’s free ATS combines unlimited jobs and users with distribution to 50+ job boards at no software cost. Tracking, scheduling, and candidate communication sit in one place, which removes the paid subscription many teams assume they need.


Dover’s Recruiting Partners add experienced, full-cycle fractional recruiters to the same system, typically averaging $4,800 per hire with no contracts, though costs vary by role seniority and hiring complexity. Because the pipeline stays in your own ATS, each search builds on the last instead of starting from zero. The same system is the layer fractional recruiting agencies are built on, which is why recruiter performance and client reviews sit alongside the pipeline data.


Sure, we’re a bit biased, but the split follows hiring volume and role complexity. With a free ATS alone, a founder still runs sourcing and screening, which can work for a handful of open roles. When several roles open at once, or a role is senior or specialized, a fractional recruiter on top of the same ATS adds capacity without a new system or a fixed salary. Fractional support tends to fit teams making roughly 5 to 50 hires a year, while a first full-time recruiter often starts to make sense around 15 to 20 hires annually.


## FAQs


### What does a startup recruiting budget typically include, and where do costs run highest?


A startup recruiting budget usually covers internal costs (ATS software, sourcing tools, internal recruiter salaries) and external costs (job board postings, background checks, and agency fees). Agency fees are where budgets get stretched fastest. At 15 to 30% of first-year salary, hiring three mid-level employees at $100k each can cost $45,000 to $90,000 in recruiter fees alone. For context,[SHRM’s 2025 benchmarking data](https://www.shrm.org/about/press-room/shrm-releases-2025-benchmarking-reports--how-does-your-organizat) puts the average non-executive cost per hire at $5,475, before any agency fee is added.


### What’s the cheapest way to hire for a startup without sacrificing candidate quality?


A free ATS paired with employee referrals and sourcing tools gets you the furthest with the least spend. Dover’s free ATS handles job posting to 50+ boards, AI-powered applicant scoring on the premium plan, and pipeline management at no software cost. Referral programs consistently produce shorter time-to-hire and stronger candidate quality than job boards or agencies, according to GetApp’s recruiter survey.


### How do fractional recruiter costs compare with percentage-based agency fees?


Traditional agencies charge a percentage of first-year salary, typically 15 to 30%, while fractional recruiters bill by the hour or per hire. Dover’s fractional recruiters average $4,800 per hire with no contracts and no minimum commitment, though costs vary by role seniority and hiring complexity. For a $100,000 role, a 15% agency fee is $15,000, a gap of roughly $10,000 per hire, and the candidate pipeline stays in your own ATS.


### How do I reduce recruiting costs without adding more software subscriptions?


Start by shifting to free tools before buying anything: a free ATS like Dover replaces paid platforms that can run thousands per year, and built-in sourcing tools replace standalone prospecting software. Layering in remote hiring expands your candidate pool without office overhead, and an employee referral program adds qualified candidates at the cost of a bonus instead of a recruiter fee.


### Can I run a full hiring process at a startup without a dedicated internal recruiter?


Yes, with the right combination of tools and on-demand support. A free ATS handles job posting, application tracking, and candidate communications, while fractional recruiters can step in for sourcing and full-cycle support on specific roles without requiring a full-time hire.


### Is a free ATS enough for an early-stage startup?


A free ATS covers job posting, application tracking, scheduling, and candidate communication, but it does not source or interview candidates for you. For teams hiring through their first 100 or so roles, that is often enough. Dover’s free ATS has no limits on jobs or users, while AI applicant scoring and the interview notetaker sit on the $199/month premium plan.


### Do I need a recruiter if I already use an ATS?


An ATS organizes the hiring process but does not source, screen, or close candidates, so that work still falls to a founder, a hiring manager, or a recruiter. For a few open roles, software with founder-led outreach can be enough. When several roles open at once, or a role is senior or specialized, a fractional recruiter can take on sourcing, screening, and closing while the hiring team keeps the hiring decisions. The arrangement tends to work best when both sides share one ATS, which gives everyone the same view of the pipeline and avoids duplicate outreach. Dover’s model pairs a free ATS with fractional recruiters averaging $4,800 per hire, though costs vary by role seniority and hiring complexity.


### What recruiting tools do Y Combinator startups tend to use?


Early-stage YC startups often run hiring through founders with no dedicated recruiter, so tooling usually needs to be free or low-cost and quick to set up. More than 100 Y Combinator startups use Dover, whose free ATS can be set up in minutes and distributes jobs to 50+ boards.


## Final Thoughts on Lowering Your Startup Recruiting Budget


Most[recruiting savings](https://www.dover.com/) come from replacing percentage-based fees and paid subscriptions with tools and models priced for the number of roles a startup actually hires, and the right mix depends on how many searches are open and how much time a founder can give them. Dover is one example of that approach, pairing a free ATS with fractional recruiters available per hire, so a team can start with software alone and bring in recruiter support only when a search calls for it.
